title: A Spire for the Thorn
premise: Cyrus Voss, last heir of the Voss smuggling guild, is dragged into a war between the surface courts and the soul-hungry court beneath Thornfell when a dying courier entrusts them with the Ember Map, which charts the only road to the Undercourt. Guided by Wren, a disgraced court mage, and hunted by both the guild that betrayed their family and the Undercourt's bone-masked riders, Cyrus learns the map was drawn by their own grandmother, who once sold her soul to buy the guild's survival. To save the last dragon, whose dying fire keeps the mountain's borders—and thousands of lives—intact, Cyrus must trade the one thing they swore never to give: their own name in the Undercourt's ledger. In the end, Cyrus outwits the ledger by erasing the Voss inheritance entirely, freeing their grandmother's soul and the dragon's fire at the cost of their family's power, choosing love with Wren over the duty of a name.
about_author: Beatrix Halloran is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction, and her love of half-remembered roads bleeds into every page she writes. She lives in a stone cottage at the edge of nowhere with two ill-tempered goats and an ever-growing collection of impossible maps.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Ledgers
chapters.summary: Cyrus Voss runs contraband through the Thornfell passes alone, the last of a guild reduced to one name on a crumbling ledger. A routine delivery goes wrong when they find a courier bleeding out in the snow. POV: Cyrus. Beat: weary isolation cracked open by sudden obligation.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Last Breath
chapters.summary: The dying courier presses a scorched map into Cyrus's hands and whispers about 'the fire under the mountain' before expiring. Bone-masked riders crest the ridge; Cyrus barely escapes down a smuggler's chute. POV: Cyrus. Beat: fear and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: In a safehouse, Cyrus studies the Ember Map and finds roads that shouldn't exist—passages into the mountain itself, marked in their grandmother's handwriting. POV: Cyrus. Beat: uncanny recognition; the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: The Guild That Isn't
chapters.summary: Cyrus seeks answers from Aunt Maren, who claims the Voss guild died twenty years ago. She recognizes the map, goes pale, and orders Cyrus to burn it. POV: Cyrus. Beat: first hint of family betrayal.

chapters.title: Ash on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Riders burn Maren's inn that night. Maren shoves Cyrus into a cellar tunnel with the map, confessing the guild sold something to the Undercourt long ago. POV: Cyrus. Beat: loss of home; the hunt begins.

chapters.title: The Mage in the Cage
chapters.summary: Fleeing through Greyhollow market, Cyrus frees a caged prisoner marked for the Undercourt: Wren, a disgraced court mage who can read the map's living ink. POV: alternating Cyrus/Wren. Beat: wary alliance forged in escape.

chapters.title: Ink That Moves
chapters.summary: Wren reveals the map redraws itself as the Undercourt shifts its halls; it will only guide someone the mountain remembers. Cyrus's blood smears on parchment make the roads glow. POV: Wren. Beat: wonder shadowed by dread—Cyrus is bound to this.

chapters.title: Bone Riders on the High Pass
chapters.summary: The bone-masked riders corner them on the Kestrel Shelf. A desperate crossing over a rotting rope bridge costs them their supplies but not their lives. POV: Cyrus. Beat: terror, and the first moment Cyrus saves Wren without thinking.

chapters.title: The Dragon's Guttering Light
chapters.summary: From a shrine on the pass they see Thornfell's peak dim—the last dragon's fire failing, and with it the wards keeping the Undercourt sealed. Villages below feel the cold. POV: Wren. Beat: stakes widen from personal to catastrophic.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Confession
chapters.summary: Hidden in the map's border, Cyrus deciphers a letter: Elira Voss sold her soul to the Undercourt to save the guild, and the debt comes due with the dragon's death. POV: Cyrus. Beat: grief and fury at inherited sin.

chapters.title: The Court Above
chapters.summary: Wren's old masters summon her; the surface court wants the map and cares nothing for souls. The pair flee royal soldiers through the flooded quarries. POV: Wren. Beat: disillusionment—duty above is as rotten as the debt below.

chapters.title: Salt and Cinder
chapters.summary: In the free-town of Saltcinder they resupply and meet Odo, an ex-Voss guildsman who confirms the betrayal: the guild elders sold Elira's contract to buy their own pardons. POV: Cyrus. Beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: By the fire, Wren admits she was cast out for trying to unmake a soul-contract once before—it killed her mentor. She offers Cyrus every chance to turn back. POV: Wren. Beat: vulnerability; the first unguarded tenderness between them.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Whisper
chapters.summary: Cyrus begins hearing the Undercourt's ledger whispering their name in dreams, each night closer than the last. The map's ink starts crawling toward their sleeping hand. POV: Cyrus. Beat: creeping horror; time is running out.

chapters.title: Riders in the Market Square
chapters.summary: Bone riders strike Saltcinder hunting the map. Odo dies holding the alley so Cyrus and Wren can escape into the deep ways. POV: Cyrus. Beat: guilt sharpening resolve; no more running.

chapters.title: The Mouth of Thornfell
chapters.summary: They reach the mountain's sealed gate, opened only by Voss blood. Cyrus cuts their palm; the stone drinks and grinds apart. POV: alternating. Beat: point of no return, entered hand in hand.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Inside, the passages shift like breathing lungs, following memories of Elira. Cyrus relives fragments of her smuggling years as the walls replay them. POV: Cyrus. Beat: intimacy with a dead grandmother; awe laced with sorrow.

chapters.title: The Hollow Fair
chapters.summary: They cross the Undercourt's border market where ghosts trade memories for warmth. A ghost-merchant warns: the ledger takes names, and a nameless one cannot leave. POV: Wren. Beat: temptation and foreshadowing of the final price.

chapters.title: Masks at the Table
chapters.summary: Invited to dine with the Undercourt's herald, they learn the court is starving since the dragon-fire wanes—it needs Elira's contract renewed by Voss blood to survive. POV: alternating. Beat: the enemy's hunger made sympathetic and more dangerous.

chapters.title: The First Bargain
chapters.summary: To reach the vault holding Elira's soul, Cyrus trades a memory of Maren. Wren is furious; trust frays. POV: Wren. Beat: conflict born of care—love against self-destruction.

chapters.title: Cold Camp in the Deep Ways
chapters.summary: Stranded by shifting roads, they shelter in a geode cavern lit by trapped lightning. Stripped of plans, they finally speak honestly and kiss. POV: alternating. Beat: tenderness as rebellion against duty.

chapters.title: The Vault of Names
chapters.summary: They breach the vault: shelves of soul-lanterns, each burning with a name. They find Elira's lantern guttering beside the dragon's stolen heartflame. POV: Cyrus. Beat: triumph curdling—both cannot be carried out.

chapters.title: Heartflame and Hook
chapters.summary: The heartflame cannot be taken without a vessel; the herald arrives with riders, offering Cyrus the guild's old pardon if they surrender Wren. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the corrupt bargain repeated across generations—refused at last.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Breathing Halls
chapters.summary: A running battle through collapsing corridors. Wren holds the ledger's wards open with her own magic, burning herself thin. POV: Wren. Beat: sacrifice offered quietly, refused just as quietly.

chapters.title: Elira's Lantern
chapters.summary: Cornered, Cyrus speaks to the lantern and Elira's voice answers, revealing the escape road she hid inside the map: the Smuggler's Road, hers alone. POV: Cyrus. Beat: inheritance reclaimed as gift, not burden.

chapters.title: The Road Only Traitors Know
chapters.summary: They take Elira's hidden way out, surfacing near the dragon's caldera—but the herald anticipated it, sealing the exit behind them. POV: alternating. Beat: hope undercut; the trap closes.

chapters.title: Fire Going Out
chapters.summary: At the caldera rim, the last dragon, Ashvane, lies dying, begging them to end it or rekindle it. Without the heartflame returned, the mountain's wards fall within days. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the weight of choice made flesh.

chapters.title: The Court Ascendant
chapters.summary: The Undercourt rises early, its spire punching through Thornfell's shoulder as the wards fail. Surface courts mobilize—not to save anyone, but to claim the spire. POV: Wren. Beat: power's corruption laid bare on all sides.

chapters.title: Terms Read by Candlelight
chapters.summary: The herald offers final terms: renew Elira's contract with a new Voss signature and the court withdraws forever. Cyrus pretends to consider. POV: Cyrus. Beat: cold clarity beneath apparent surrender.

chapters.title: What a Name Is Worth
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Wren plan the true gambit: contracts bind names, so Cyrus will strike the Voss name from the ledger entirely, voiding every Voss pact—including the pardon that built the guild. POV: alternating. Beat: love and resolve fused into strategy.

chapters.title: Descent to the Spire
chapters.summary: They walk openly into the risen spire under flag of parley, Cyrus carrying the heartflame as bait. The court's starving beauty surrounds them. POV: Cyrus. Beat: dread transfigured into ceremony.

chapters.title: Before the Ledger
chapters.summary: In the ledger hall, Cyrus signs the renewal—then, as the ink binds, drives the quill through the Voss entry, invoking the ghost-market law: a name freely erased voids its debts. POV: Cyrus. Beat: climax; everything staked on a technicality bought with memory.

chapters.title: The Unraveling
chapters.summary: Every Voss contract unravels: the guild's pardons, the elders' bargains, Elira's sale. Freed souls stream upward like sparks; the enraged court turns on Cyrus. POV: Wren. Beat: chaos, elation, and immediate peril.

chapters.title: Ashvane Wakes
chapters.summary: Wren carries the heartflame up the spire's throat while Cyrus holds the herald off with Elira's smuggler tricks. At the caldera, the flame returns and Ashvane ignites, flooding the mountain with new fire. POV: alternating. Beat: the turn—fire answering courage.

chapters.title: The Spire Falls Silent
chapters.summary: Rekindled wards crush the Undercourt back into the deep; the spire crumbles to glass. The herald, unmasked, is revealed as the first Voss elder, still serving his ancient bargain. POV: Cyrus. Beat: horror and pity entwined.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: With the Voss line struck out, Cyrus is legally no one—free of duty, inheritance, and the court's reach. Maren, alive after all, finds them and weeps at what was done to save them. POV: Cyrus. Beat: grief and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Court Above Comes Calling
chapters.summary: The surface crown offers Cyrus lands and title for 'resolving' the crisis—an attempt to own the miracle. Cyrus declines publicly, handing the credit to the dead. POV: Wren. Beat: power refused; corruption starved.

chapters.title: A Guild of Two
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Wren found no guild at all—just a road-mending partnership, guiding refugees around the wounded mountain. The Ember Map, its purpose served, fades to blank vellum. POV: alternating. Beat: quiet rebuilding; love as daily practice.

chapters.title: Sparks on the Wind
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, freed souls including Elira rise past the caldera in a visible river of light. Cyrus says goodbye properly at last. POV: Cyrus. Beat: mourning completed; gratitude replacing anger.

chapters.title: A Spire for the Thorn
chapters.summary: Years later, travelers tell of two wardens of Thornfell who keep the passes safe and ask no names. On the peak, a new spire of dragon-glass catches the dawn—raised not for power, but as a promise kept. POV: Cyrus, closing. Beat: peace earned; the thorn crowned in light.
